title: Breast Implant Drop and Fluff: Timeline, Week by Week
meta_description: Drop and fluff can take 3 to 6 months. You begin to notice final results around 3 months, with subtle changes to 12. What changes, and when to call.
excerpt: Implants sit high and tight at first, then settle. You begin to notice your final results around 3 months, and the whole process can take 3 to 6 months. Here is what each stage looks like, what can slow it down, and when to call your surgeon.
quick_answer:
How long does it take for implants to drop and fluff?

An article on the ASPS website says the whole drop and fluff process can take 3 to 6 months. University of Utah Health says you begin to notice your final results around 3 months, with subtle changes through 12 months. Smaller or textured implants may take longer, and one side may settle before the other.

staged_replacement.text_in_image:
Breast Implants: Drop + Fluff Timeline
The whole process can take 3–6 months.
1) Drop: The implant moves to a lower, more natural-looking position.
2) Fluff: The implant fills out the lower breast. The shape gets softer and rounder.
Week 1: High and tight
Weeks 2–3: Starting to settle
Weeks 4–6: Softer, may still sit high
Months 2–3: Final results begin to show around month 3
Months 3–6: The process can finish
Up to 12 months: Subtle changes only
Timing varies. Sources: articles on the ASPS website; University of Utah Health.

sources.title: What does "drop and fluff" mean after breast augmentation?
quotes: The entire drop and fluff process can take three to six months to complete
Initial swelling and bruising should subside in one to two weeks after getting breast implants.
With this, your muscles should begin to relax, allowing your implants to gradually settle and soften.
you might notice that your implants are "riding high" on your chest and may look flatter than you'd hoped or slightly square in shape.
These are normal occurrences caused by tight skin and muscle tissue that will gradually resolve as your implants drop and fluff over the coming weeks.

As tight muscles relax and acclimate to your new implants, you can expect your implants to "drop" to a lower, more natural-looking position on your chest, as well as "fluff," or fill out the lower area of your breasts.
This process will give way to a smoother, softer and more rounded final appearance
Your breast implants may appear to be bigger or fuller once they've dropped to a lower, more natural-looking position on your chest
You might notice that the appearance of your new implants changes several times before your final results settle in.
Before you spring for a new wardrobe, though, give your breasts several months to settle into place and for their size and shape to stop adjusting.
While there is little you can do to make your implants drop and fluff faster
Smaller, lighter implants, for example, may take longer than heavier implants to drop and fluff
if you have textured breast implants, you may see a more gradual drop and fluff process than with smooth implants
If your breast implants are taking longer than expected to settle into place, don't panic.
In most cases, breast implants will drop and fluff – whether gradually or more dramatically – over the course of three to six months after your procedure.
If this does not appear to be happening or if you are experiencing any problems such as unusual pain, bleeding or swelling that does not go down or is getting worse
